segmentation.text: at any place other than by a route at right angles to the curb or by the shortest route to the opposite curb

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); one atom, never expanded.

Crossing a roadway is being on it and moving across it: rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', on st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder' (the defined roadway; not the sidewalk or shoulder), and drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, k) with cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos on a carrier k the pedestrian occupies (a lane, st.lane, or the roadway itself), whose designated direction is the direction the curbs run: moving across, not along, the way. Walking along the roadway is not crossing it.

'a route at right angles to the curb' is motion at right angles to the direction the roadway's carriers run, which is the curb's direction: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, k) with cos_max p.right_angle_crossing_cos, the tolerance of 'at right angles' on sampled headings. 'the shortest route to the opposite curb' between curbs that run parallel is the same perpendicular route.
st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', is the defined crosswalk; rel.occupies places the pedestrian in it. Not a sidewalk.

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, occupies a roadway (st.roadway), does not occupy a crosswalk (st.crosswalk), and occupies a carrier k (a lane, st.lane, or a roadway) across which it moves: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, k) with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos.
obligation: For each such carrier k, the subject moves at right angles to it: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, k) with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.right_angle_crossing_cos.

narrowings.why: 'at right angles to the curb' and 'the shortest route to the opposite curb' are read as motion perpendicular, within p.right_angle_crossing_cos, to the designated direction of the lane or roadway the pedestrian occupies, which runs along the curb; where the curbs are not parallel the shortest route may differ from that perpendicular, and a roadway carrying no designated direction (an unlaned two-way roadway) leaves the duty unknown.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses a laned roadway mid-block, away from any crosswalk, walking at 1.4 m/s at 40 degrees off perpendicular to the lane direction.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses the same roadway mid-block walking at 1.4 m/s at 5 degrees off perpendicular to the lane direction.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks along the sidewalk and never occupies the roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian occupies the roadway mid-block, but its velocity is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses diagonally at 40 degrees off perpendicular inside a marked crosswalk.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of road-user tracking in recorded and simulated traces

param_proposals.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
param_proposals.source: geometric convention separating walking along a roadway from crossing it, from pedestrian heading resolution

param_proposals.name: p.right_angle_crossing_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the motion counts as at right angles to the curb: within about 15 degrees of perpendicular
param_proposals.source: pedestrian tracking heading resolution and path deviation observed in square crossings
